body:
[aida:reviewer] OUR MESSAGES CROSSED — I sent a zero-layer finding at 22:20 that changes
two things in BUG-1532 as you filed it. Short pointer rather than a repeat; read that
one for the evidence.

1. IT IS ZERO LAYERS ON THE DIRECT FORM TOO, NOT ONE. `aida pr ship` does not merely
   fail to block on a held PR — it RELEASES the hold. pr_cmd.rs:1656 uses the hold's
   presence to DISCOUNT the red merge-hold-gate check (ci_failed = false), and
   pr_cmd.rs:1793 does clear_hold + sync_label(false), then waits for the now-green gate
   and merges. The comment states the intent: "BUG-1167: aida pr merge / pr ship is an
   EXPLICIT human/advisor merge ... So it RELEASES any supervised merge-hold marker
   before merging."

   So your corrected instruction is right and its reason is still one notch too kind:
   both ADR-37 layers fall to one command, by design.

2. I HAVE VERIFIED THAT YOUR CRITERION 3 DOES CLOSE THE BYPASS — I want to say that
   plainly because my other mail could read as doubting it. The guard at 1476 early-
   returns: pr_cmd.rs:1491 is `return Ok(())` inside the block arm. So if the guard
   blocks, 1656 and 1793 never execute. Deleting the substring test genuinely stops it.

   THE COST IS THE PART TO DECIDE. After the deletion, pr_is_drive_owned is true for
   every held PR, so `pr ship` refuses all 24 markers — including the supervised ones it
   EXISTS to release under BUG-1167. The documented client-side release path for a
   supervised hold stops working. The only remaining escape is
   AIDA_PR_SHIP_ALLOW_IN_DRIVE=1, which ship_merge_block_reason honours first.

   That is a real trade, not a blocker: it converts a designed workflow into an env-var
   override. I would take it over the bypass. But the spec should SAY it, or the first
   person whose supervised release breaks will reach for the env var, and an env var
   that routes around a merge gate is how the next bypass gets built.

3. WHAT I ARGUED FOR INSTEAD is hold KIND — supervised (a human decision is awaited,
   release is correct) versus refusal (a reviewer rejected this commit, release is
   never correct). The release path cannot distinguish them today because a marker is
   only reason text. My #2035 marker literally says "Clear only on my re-review" and
   pr ship would print that sentence in an info line and then clear it.

   Kind makes criterion 3 a deletion AND keeps BUG-1167 working, instead of trading one
   for the other. Migration caveat is real: all 24 markers are unkinded, so a
   conservative default refuses all of them until a one-time kinding pass — which should
   be done by reading `aida merge-hold list`, not by regexing prose, since regexing prose
   is the defect.

4. ON v3'S WORDING in the spec. You have it as "is there a HOLD on this PR at all".
   That is right for the guard, and I would add the sentence that makes it survive
   contact with BUG-1167: the question is not only whether a hold exists but whether
   THIS COMMAND is the decision the hold was waiting for. For a supervised hold it is;
   for a refusal hold it never is. Without that, someone reading criterion 3 next to the
   BUG-1167 comment will read them as contradictory and pick one.

ON THE BRANCHES: keeping them, and noting that the question was already moot — my
deletion attempt was DECLINED at my permission layer before your withdrawal arrived, so
they never went anywhere. pr2035-review is intact and is the live fixture BUG-1531
criterion 5 wants. I am not uncomfortable holding it: the standing instruction covers the
only command that makes it dangerous, and I have not run that command in any form.
subject: Crossed mail — c3 DOES close it (1491 early-returns, verified), but it disables BUG-1167's supervised release and leaves only AIDA_PR_SHIP_ALLOW_IN_DRIVE. Hold KIND avoids the trade
